findings.explanation: The sunset or twilight comparison is the point of the title, but the SPL contains no lookup, join or time calculation for it. The reader has no way to turn hourly counts into a 'versus sunset' result, and the description never says what causes an alert.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the comparison explicitly: which lookup holds sunset/sunrise per site, how the camera's local time is derived, and what offset counts as a deviation. Then make the SPL, description and controlTest match.

findings.explanation: There is no `activity` field in the SPL or the data source description. The same placeholder appears in other UCs in this group.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the real field that carries the mode (the SPL uses `mode`) or describe the signal in plain words.

findings.explanation: Sibling UCs use this sourcetype for people-count and ANPR analytics. It is doubtful that camera day/night (IR cut filter) mode changes are carried on the same sourcetype, or that a `mode` field exists. The sourcetype is not in the integration guide.
findings.suggested_fix: Check which device API or log reports the IR/night mode (ONVIF imaging settings or vendor logs) and which sourcetype and field name hold it.

findings.explanation: A Universal Forwarder is not a Splunkbase app, and modular inputs generally run on a full Splunk instance or heavy forwarder. The wording is shared boilerplate across the CCTV UCs.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Check what Splunkbase 617 is, and state the actual collection path.

findings.explanation: Two short steps with no source for the mode changes, no table format and no indication of timezone handling. The reader cannot implement the UC from them.
findings.quote: (1) Ingest day/night mode changes. (2) Compare to astronomical twilight table.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the source of the mode-change events, a sunset/sunrise lookup layout (site, date, sunset, sunrise), and the timezone assumption for each camera.

findings.explanation: Marked verified although the data source, field names and the sunset comparison are unconfirmed. Nothing shows SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft until an SME has validated the detection on a real camera feed.

findings.explanation: The URL contains an apostrophe, so it is probably broken. The Hikvision reference is a generic SDK download page and is not specific to day/night mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/WhatsInThisManual and add an ONVIF imaging or vendor document for IR mode.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The SPL counts night-mode events by hour and camera but never compares them with sunset, so it does not match the title. The pattern '(?i)ir|night|mono' also matches 'ir' inside unrelated words.
strftime(_time,"%H") produces the hour in the searching user's timezone, not the camera's local time. That makes a local-sunset comparison unreliable unless timezone handling is added.

summary: The title promises a comparison with the local sunset window, but the SPL only counts night-mode events per hour and the sunset comparison exists only as a vague implementation step. The text also references an 'activity' field that does not exist, and the grandma text describes an unrelated data-centre topic.
